SELECTED_INDEX: 10
CONFIDENCE: 0.78
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows an aryl + aliphatic pattern: dual C–H stretches at 3073 (aromatic) and 2972 cm⁻¹ (aliphatic) consistent with Ar–CH and CH2 groups (GFQ-003). Two very strong bands at 1266 and 1094 cm⁻¹ match the typical pair of C–O stretching modes of an aryl–alkyl ether (asymmetric aryl–O ~1250–1270; symmetric/alkyl–O ~1080–1120), which specifically supports an Ar–O–CH2 moiety present only in candidate 10. The para-disubstituted benzene signature is evident from the CH out-of-plane doublet at 835/810 cm⁻¹. Halogen stretches are consistent with both Br and Cl: a strong band at 506 cm⁻¹ (aryl C–Br) and bands at 636–672 cm⁻¹ (C–Cl). The weak band at 1445 cm⁻¹ fits CH2 scissoring. Altogether, these features uniquely favor the p-bromophenyl chloromethyl ether (candidate 10) over benzyl halides lacking an ether.
